_about.bytes: every binary value is standard base64 with padding; hex is lowercase
deterministic_but_swift_verified: envelope (non-captured part) is built by this test with a fixed ephemeral key and nonce through the same HKDF/AES-GCM calls as KeyEnvelope.seal, and KeyEnvelope.open(as:from:) is asserted to recover thread_key from it.
thread_crypto.primitive and thread_crypto.turn_record use AES.GCM.seal with an explicit nonce; ThreadCrypto.open is asserted to open every ciphertext.
_about.fixed_inputs: all randomness is replaced by the fixed bytes given beside each vector; 32-byte seeds are SHA-256 of the label in `seed_label` and are also given raw
_about.memory_records_note: LEDGER-WIRE §13.2–§13.5 (slice 2½). `key` is the `moe:memory` keyring entry, seed_label moe.vectors.memory-key. claim_assert and document are sealed with it exactly as thread_crypto seals a turn (AES-256-GCM, combined = nonce || ciphertext || tag, base64; the nonce is given). claim_assert.claim_id is Claim.id(target, normalise(text)) over the PLAINTEXT (claim-conformance.json has the id vectors); the record body carries it as `claim`, never `id` — §13.4's example says `id`, the writers say `claim`. claim_retract carries the id and no text. document.body is exactly {name, bytes, enc, text_enc}: NO sha256 on the wire (a hash of a small dictionary is the dictionary; GCM already authenticates) — a reader hashes the plaintext it opened, and document.text_sha256_hex is that value for checking. bytes is the plaintext's UTF-8 length; a removal is bytes 0 and text_enc "" (document_removed). A `claim` whose text_enc is "" is malformed and not a claim (ignored by every reader), while a `document` whose text_enc is "" is the removal marker. plaintext_claim is a `claim` with `text` and no `text_enc`: every implementation must classify it as plaintext (§13.3, carriesPlaintext / Record.is_plaintext / the edge's 400 plaintext_body) and must NOT classify claim_assert, claim_retract, document or document_removed as plaintext. None of these records carries a `thread`.
_about.records_note: in records[].input, `prev: null` means the key is ABSENT from the record (LEDGER-WIRE §1.2, §10.9); `double_keys` lists body keys whose values are Doubles in Swift even where the JSON here shows an integer (1.0 -> 1).
round_trip_only: introduction.captured.signature — CryptoKit Ed25519 signing is randomised (see json_details.ed25519_signing_deterministic); Python must VERIFY this signature over introduction.signed_bytes with signer_signing_public, and its own signatures must verify the same way. The signed bytes are deterministic.

envelope.captured.sealed_by_swift — a full KeyEnvelope.seal output (random ephemeral key and AES-GCM nonce); Python must open it with envelope.recipient_agreement_private and recover envelope.thread_key.

thread_crypto.captured.turn_record — a `turn` record as ConversationProjector.turnBody writes it (random AES-GCM nonces); Python must check the id and decrypt text_enc / tools_enc with thread_crypto.captured.turn_record.key.

record_signature.captured.signature — LEDGER-WIRE §12.1: Ed25519 by signer_signing_private over record_signature.signed_bytes (deterministic: "moe.record.v1" || 0x00 || the record's canonical bytes). Python must verify it with signer_signing_public, and its own `sig` must verify the same way. record_signature.captured.wire_object is the §11 Record object as pushed, with `sig`.

memory_records.captured.claim_assert / .document — the same two records as written by the production writers (ClaimLedger.assert, DocumentRecord.append) with random nonces; Python must check the id and decrypt text_enc with memory_records.key to the stated `text`.

sas.code_layout: 120 bits big-endian, 5 bits per char MSB-first into the alphabet, 24 chars in 6 groups of 4 joined by '-'
sas.salt_note: no salt (HKDF<SHA256>.deriveKey without salt) = RFC 5869 empty salt

ticket.note: hash = SHA-256("moe.enrol.ticket.v1" || 0x00 || upper(ticket) with '-' and ' ' removed)

captured.note: Ed25519 over signed_bytes by signer_signing_private; not deterministic in CryptoKit — verify, do not compare

base64.note: Data(base64Encoded:) with default options, which is what ThreadCrypto.open, ThreadKeyring and DeviceIdentity.load use

json_details.control_character_note: json = what appears between the quotes for a one-character string under the canonical options; escaped = it begins with a backslash
json_details.doubles_note: keys are the Swift Double literal; values are the exact JSON text Foundation emits
json_details.ed25519_note: CryptoKit's Curve25519.Signing produces a different signature each call (randomised, RFC 8032 verification still applies); signatures are round-trip-only
json_details.jsonvalue_note: a Double 1.0 is written as `1` and so re-reads as an Int; the canonical bytes (and the id) are unchanged, only the Swift enum case differs
json_details.key_order_note: what .sortedKeys does for mixed-case, digit, punctuation, empty, space and non-ASCII keys. It is NOT code-point order: Foundation sorts with NSString.compare options [.numeric, .caseInsensitive, .forcedOrdering] under the system locale (9 < 10, a < A < ä, punctuation before digits before letters). Python must reproduce key_order_sample byte for byte, so json.dumps(sort_keys=True) alone is only correct when every key is lowercase ASCII letters and '_' with no digits and no key that is a prefix-plus-punctuation of another.

timestamp.parse_note: LedgerRecord.parse(timestamp:); reformatted = what the hash would then be computed over (LEDGER-WIRE §1.3, §10.10)

claim_assert.note: written by Claim.body(sealedWith:) with a random nonce; same inputs as memory_records.claim_assert

document.note: written by DocumentRecord.body with a random nonce; same inputs as memory_records.document

claim_assert.name: sealed_claim_assert
claim_assert.note: §13.4: a `claim` assert with text sealed under moe:memory; no `thread`; `key` and `source` in the clear

claim_retract.name: claim_retract
claim_retract.note: §13.4: a retract carries the claim id and no text; `after` names the assert

document.name: document
document.note: §13.5: a `document` — name, the plaintext's UTF-8 byte count, text sealed under moe:memory; no `thread`, and no hash of the words on the wire (text_sha256_hex is what a reader computes after opening)

document_removed.name: document_removed
document_removed.note: §13.5: bytes 0 and text_enc "" — the file is removed; readable with no key (on a `claim` the same text_enc is malformed, not a removal)

plaintext_claim.name: plaintext_claim
plaintext_claim.note: §13.3: `text` and no `text_enc` — plaintext, whatever the kind; not pushed, not adopted, 400 plaintext_body

captured.note: Ed25519 over signed_bytes by signer_signing_private; not deterministic in CryptoKit — verify, do not compare. wire_object is the §11 Record object as it goes over POST /v1/ledger/push: the file form plus `sig`.

record_signature.note: LEDGER-WIRE §12.1: sig = Ed25519(author's signing key, "moe.record.v1" || 0x00 || canonical bytes of §1.2). sig is a sidecar: not in the canonical form, not in the id, not on the .jsonl line; on the §11 Record object it is the `sig` key, base64. A verifier re-derives the id and checks sig over the same buffer, under the key its OWN peer book holds for record.device.

records.name: ascii_first_record
records.note: ASCII only; first record on its device (prev absent, after empty); timestamp with .000 ms; a `/` in a string; thread.delete-like body

records.name: non_ascii
records.note: é (U+00E9), an emoji outside the BMP (U+1F600), Hebrew; prev present; after non-empty; timestamp with .999 ms

records.name: control_characters
records.note: every code point U+0000–U+001F, then U+007F, U+2028, U+2029, in one string field (and again as a JSON key)

records.name: keys_differing_by_case_and_sort_order
records.note: body keys that differ only by case, plus digits/underscore/non-ASCII keys, to pin .sortedKeys ordering (LEDGER-WIRE §10.1)

records.name: doubles
records.note: 1.5, 1.0, 1e21, 0.1, 1e-7, 1e100, 123456789.125 as JSONValue.double (the app never writes doubles; LEDGER-WIRE §10.3)

records.name: prev_present_after_empty

records.name: prev_absent_after_nonempty
